alt: A bar chart of maximum sentences. Life for robbery, aggravated burglary, arson and criminal damage endangering life; 14 years for burglary of a dwelling, blackmail and handling; 10 years for burglary of another building, criminal damage and fraud; 7 years for theft; 5 years for obtaining services dishonestly; 2 years for making off without payment.
caption: Force, weapons and danger to life push the maximum to life; making off is the lowest at two years.

alt: Four questions for robbery: a completed theft (Robinson); force or fear of force (Dawson and James, Clouden, but not P v DPP); at the time, with appropriation continuing while making off (Hale); and in order to steal with the mens rea of theft. All four give robbery, with a maximum of life.
caption: No theft, no robbery; and the force must be used in order to steal.

alt: Blackmail needs a demand (made on posting, Treacy v DPP) with menaces (R v Clear; R v Garwood) and a view to gain or intent to cause loss. The demand is unwarranted unless the defendant believes both that there are reasonable grounds for it and that the menaces are a proper way to reinforce it; a threat of serious crime can never be believed proper (R v Harvey).
caption: Demand, menaces, gain or loss, and no belief that both the demand and the menaces were proper.

alt: Four criminal damage offences: s1(1) damage, with Hardman, A v R and R v Smith; s1(2) endangering life and s1(3) arson, with a maximum of life; s2 threats; s3 possession. The s5 lawful excuse covers an honest belief in the owner’s consent (Jaggard v Dickinson) or in protecting property by reasonable means (Hill and Hall), but not offences endangering life.
caption: An honest belief in consent or in protecting property is a lawful excuse, except where life is endangered.

alt: A timeline of Mo’s actions. Entering with intent to steal completes burglary under s9(1)(a), because intent to steal exceeds his permission as a customer (Jones and Smith). Pocketing the ring is theft under ss1 to 6 (Ivey). Pushing the assistant while running out is force at the time of the theft because appropriation continues (Hale), so robbery is likely.
caption: Burglary on entry, theft on pocketing, robbery when he pushes past.
